title_original: MOP Foundation : David Sims : The Photographer, Fashion and the Hamster
excerpt_original: Since his beginnings, David Sims has kept one eye in the viewfinder and the other on the spirit of the times. Born in Sheffield […] Cet article MOP Foundation : David Sims : The Photographer, Fashion and the Hamster est apparu en premier sur The Eye of Photography Magazine .

blocks.text: Since his beginnings, David Sims has kept one eye in the viewfinder and the other on the spirit of the times. Born in Sheffield in 1966, the British photographer has regularly shaken up the fashion world. He moves with ease between commissioned editorials for the specialist press and major advertising campaigns, without ever setting aside his personal research or his taste for the road less traveled. This front-rank recognition has translated into the entry of his prints into the permanent collections of major museum institutions, from the Victoria and Albert Museum in London to the Tate, by way of LACMA in Los Angeles.

A keen connoisseur of the history of his medium and its great aesthetic currents, David Sims has also always stayed ahead of technical developments. As early as the late 1990s, just as his career was taking off, he had already grasped the full significance of the coming digital age. It is, moreover, at this pivotal moment, where the guiding thread of his last thirty years of work took shape, that the exhibition begins.

With The Hamster Becomes The Problem , the photographer opens the doors to his vast archives a little. “It’s often by accident that I come across my old work; for this exhibition, it’s as if someone had turned out my boxes, rummaged through the pile and made a selection.” Navigating by instinct between the world of fashion and a quasi-documentary approach, between stolen moments and pure studio staging, between fervor and moments of tenderness, the hang reveals an artist who, in his own words, chose “a more peripheral creativity.”

Far from a simple chronological survey, The Hamster Becomes The Problem simulates a stroll through a series of interlinked environments, each revealing a facet of the photographer’s visual universe. Ever attentive to the trends of our collective imaginations, he gives form to singular characters who embody the aesthetic of our time.

“David Sims has always known that photography goes beyond the mere frame of the image,” says Marta Ortega Pérez, founder and president of the MOP Foundation, who knows the artist well. “Since his beginnings, his photographs have gathered the faces, attitudes and cultural movements that have shaped entire generations, composing a body of work that has lost none of its influence or relevance today. At the heart of his approach lies a deep connection with youth culture, whose raw energy, vulnerability, creativity and constant need to reinvent itself he captures with precision. Few photographers have observed these social and aesthetic upheavals with such finesse, or grasped so instinctively how much they change the way we see ourselves and our own cultural environment. The exhibition offers a unique chance to approach this work from David’s own point of view, and to follow the stories and the characters that animate the work of this great storyteller in images.”

Sims remains very lucid about the ephemeral nature of his activity, which he even embraces, and, given the ironic title of his exhibition, he no doubt compares himself to that hamster running endlessly on the wheel of its cage until exhaustion, metaphorically taking the angle of a fashion world so entrenched in the infernal consumption cycles of our capitalist societies.

“ The Hamster Becomes The Problem ” opens on November 21, 2026 and runs through May 1, 2027 at the MOP Foundation in A Coruña (Spain). Curated by Charlotte Cotton. Information: https://themopfoundation.org/en/exhibitions/david-sims
